findings.title: Dashboard Capture card fires the OLD exposure while displaying the new one (typed value only commits on Enter)
findings.what_happened: In the Capture dashboard widget I clicked the Exp field, selected all, typed 2, pressed Tab, then pressed Capture. The field kept showing 'Exp: 2' but the native log recorded 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1' and the progress ring read 13% after ~16 s (13% of 120 s = 15.6 s - exact match). Typing the same value and pressing Enter instead did commit (the field renormalised to '3.0' and the capture ran ~3 s). So the card can show one exposure and take a completely different one, indefinitely, with no warning.
findings.expected: Losing focus (Tab, clicking another control, pressing Capture) must commit the edit, or the field must visibly reject/revert the uncommitted text. What the card shows and what it captures must never disagree.
findings.repro: Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Capture Settings -> Done. Click the Exp box, Ctrl+A, type 2, press Tab, press Capture. Watch the progress % and `grep 'Starting.*exposure' /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log`.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-38.png: field reads 'Exp: 2' while the ring reads 13% of a run the log calls 120 s. /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log 18:42:16 'Starting 120s exposure'. Repeated with Tab at a different value (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-41.png: field '2', progress 90% of the previously committed 9 s).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/capture_settings_card.dart:536 - _CompactSettingField wires only `onSubmitted: widget.onChanged`; there is no onEditingComplete/onChanged and no FocusNode listener. didUpdateWidget (:478) only rewrites the controller when the provider value changes, so stale text survives forever. Both Exp and Gain use this field.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a FocusNode and commit on focus loss (and on onEditingComplete), or switch to onChanged with debounce. Also re-read the controller text in the Capture handler before dispatching.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Fresh v-wizards profile, Simulated Camera+Mount+Filter Wheel connected, Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Capture Settings. Clicked the Exp box (default 120.0), Ctrl+A, typed 2, pressed Tab (focus visibly moved to Gain, field still read '2' - /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-21.png), pressed Capture. app.log: 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-22.png shows the card reading 'Exp: 2' beside a 10% ring - 10% of 120 s = 12 s, matching wall clock since the log line, so the ring is timing the 120 s run, not a 2 s one. Control: repeating with Enter instead of Tab renormalised the field to '3.0' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-23.png), i.e. the commit path works and only the blur path is missing. Cited location is correct: capture_settings_card.dart:536 is `onSubmitted: widget.onChanged` inside _CompactSettingField (class at :449), with no onEditingComplete, no onChanged and no FocusNode; didUpdateWidget at :478 only overwrites the controller when the provider value changes, so the stale text survives indefinitely. Both Exp and Gain use this field. P1 is right - it is silent and unbounded (the card can disagree with the hardware forever), but it needs a user to leave the field by blur rather than Enter, which keeps it below P0.

findings.repro: Fresh profile -> skip onboarding -> Equipment -> connect Simulated Camera/Mount/Focuser/Filter Wheel (no weather, no safety monitor) -> Dashboard. Right column, SAFETY tile.

findings.proposed_fix: Make the badge a three-state derived from the data source: safe (fresh reading, safe), unsafe (fresh reading, unsafe), unmonitored (no source or stale). Never fall back to 'Safe' as the default when isSafe is null/absent.

findings.title: Dashboard Mount jog pad fires a 500 ms pulse guide instead of a slew - the arrows do nothing a user can see
findings.what_happened: The Mount Control dashboard widget shows an N/S/E/W arrow pad that looks like a slew/jog pad. Each press calls mountCommandService.pulseGuide(direction), which the native log shows as 'Pulse guiding sim_mount_1 for 500ms in direction east' - about 4 arcseconds at guide rate. RA/Dec on the card stayed at 00:00:00 / +00d00'00" across three presses, no toast, no status change. Press-and-hold for 2 s produced exactly one 500 ms pulse, not a continuous slew.
findings.expected: An arrow pad on a mount control card should slew (moveAxis / directional slew) at a user-selectable rate while held, as it does in NINA, SGP and the ASIAIR, and stop on release. If it really is a guide pulse it must be labelled as one and show the resulting offset.
findings.repro: Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> enable Mount Control -> Done -> Unpark -> click the E arrow, then press-and-hold it for 2 s. Watch RA on the card and `tail /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log`.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log: '18:37:41 Pulse guiding sim_mount_1 for 500ms in direction east', '18:37:57 ... 500ms ...' (that one was a 2 s hold), '18:38:35 ... 500ms ...'. Card RA unchanged in /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-30.png and -31.png.
findings.proposed_fix: Bind the pad to a hold-to-slew (start on pointer down, stop on pointer up/cancel) using the mount's directional slew, and add a slew-rate selector next to the existing tracking-rate selector.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly on the rebuilt bundle. Enabled the Mount Control tile, connected the sim mount, unparked; one click on the E chevron produced a single native log line '2026-08-03T20:48:05 INFO Pulse guiding sim_mount_1 for 500ms in direction east' and the card's RA stayed 00h 00m 00s. Press-and-hold via xdotool mousedown/2.5s/mouseup produced EXACTLY ONE further 500 ms pulse, not a continuous slew (counted 'Pulse guiding' lines appended to /tmp/ns-audit/v2-wizards/app.log). Location is exact: mount_control_card.dart:173-182 is the _MountDirectionalPad construction, :176 'onDirection: (direction) async {', :179 '.pulseGuide(direction);'. mount_command_service.dart:375 is 'Future<CommandActionResult> pulseGuide(String direction, {int durationMs = 500})' and the card never passes a duration, so every press is the 500 ms default.

findings.title: Tonight card reports a concrete twilight time and 9h28m imaging window while saying 'Location needed'
findings.what_happened: With no observing location set (app_settings.observer_latitude = 0.0, and the command-bar LST reads '--:--:--'), the Tonight dashboard card shows Twilight 15:22, Moon 90%, Window 9h 28m - and in the same card Target: 'Location needed' plus 'Set an observing location to generate target plans.' The twilight/window numbers are computed at latitude 0 / longitude 0 in the machine's local timezone (15:22 local = 19:22 UTC, which is astronomical twilight on the equator on Aug 1), so they are wrong for every real observer, and there is no marking that they are placeholders.
findings.expected: Twilight and Window must render as '--' (like LST and Exposure already do) until a site is set. A user reading 'Window 9h 28m' will plan a session around a number that is not theirs.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, skip onboarding, do not set an observing location. Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Tonight -> Done. Read the Tonight tile.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-34.png (Twilight 15:22, Window 9h 28m, Target 'Location needed'); sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/data/skotiq.db "select key,value from app_settings where key like '%latitude%'" -> observer_latitude|0.0; command bar shows LST '--:--:--' in the same frame.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the twilight/window rows on the same 'has site' predicate the Target row already uses, and render '--' when it is false. Never fall back to lat/lon 0,0.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live: fresh profile, onboarding skipped, no site set. Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Tonight. The card (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-14.png) reads Twilight 15:21, Moon 84%, Window 9h 28m, Target 'Location needed', Exposure '--', with the command bar LST showing '-:-:-' in the same frame. DB agrees: observer_latitude|0.0, observer_longitude|0.0, observer_elevation|0.0. I recomputed the numbers independently rather than comparing two of the app's own readouts: for lat 0 / lon 0 on 2026-08-02 the sun crosses -18 deg at 19:22 UTC (dusk) and 04:51 UTC (dawn), i.e. 15:22 and 00:51 local on this machine, giving a 9h29m dark window. The app's 15:21/15:22 and 9h28m are exactly the equator-at-Greenwich values in local time, so the stated CAUSE is right, not just the symptom. Source confirms: tonight_card.dart:76-107 formats twilight.astronomicalDusk/Dawn with no location gate; only Target (:69) and Exposure (:154) degrade to a placeholder. P1 held - 'Window 9h 28m' is a number a user plans a night around.

findings.title: Polar alignment ends with a green "Alignment Complete" tick and a green "+0%" chip after a 30-arcminute residual error
findings.what_happened: I ran Three-Point Polar Alignment to completion against the simulators (camera+mount connected, ASTAP stub solving). Three points measured, adjust phase entered, then I pressed Done. The result screen shows a large green success check, the headline 'Alignment Complete', 'Final error: 1800.0 arcseconds', and an Alignment Summary reading Before 1800" -> After 1800" with Improvement rendered as a GREEN '+0%' chip. The Alignment History row for the run is likewise stamped with a green checkmark ('Today 10:30 / Final: 1800" / +0%'). 1800 arcsec is 30 arcminutes - half a degree of polar error, 60x the wizard's own Auto-Complete threshold of 30" - and the session improved the alignment by exactly nothing.
findings.expected: The terminal state must be honest about the residual. Success styling (green tick, green chip) belongs only to a run that reached the configured threshold. A run that ends 60x above threshold with 0% improvement should read 'Alignment stopped - still 30' 00" off' in amber/red, and the improvement chip should be neutral or red at <=0%.
findings.repro: Equipment -> connect Simulated Camera + Simulated Mount. Imaging -> Mount tab -> Three-Point Polar Alignment -> Start Alignment. Let the 3 points measure, wait for the adjust phase, press Done.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-116.png (green check, 'Alignment Complete', Final error 1800.0 arcseconds, Before 1800" -> After 1800", green +0%). /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-118.png (history row, green tick, +0%). DB agrees: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/data/skotiq.db 'select initial_total_error,final_total_error,auto_completed from polar_alignment_history' -> 1800.00067|1800.00062|0. auto_completed=0 is recorded, so the app KNOWS the threshold was never met, and still renders success.
findings.proposed_fix: Drive the completion iconography and the history-row icon off `auto_completed` / (final_total_error <= autoCompleteThreshold), not off 'the task ended'. Colour the improvement chip by sign: green only for a real reduction, neutral at 0, red if the error grew.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced the completion screen end to end. TPPA with Simulated Camera+Mount: three points measured and solved, adjust phase entered with the rail reading Az 1412.4" / Alt -1603.0" / Total 2136.5" in red, then pressed Done. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-33.png: large green success check, 'Alignment Complete', 'Final error: 1800.0 arcseconds', 'Before 1800" -> After 1800"', and an Improvement chip rendered '+0%' in green. DB shows the app knew better: polar_alignment_history row 2 = 1800.00129188552|1800.00131984104|0 - auto_completed=0 and the residual got very slightly WORSE. 1800" = 30 arcmin = 60x the wizard's own 30" threshold. Source is unconditional: _buildCompleteStatus() always paints Icon(SkotiqIcons.success, color: colors.success) + 'Alignment Complete', and _buildCompletionSummary() always paints the improvement badge with tintedBadge(colors.success) and text colour colors.success - no threshold or sign test (only the thin bar behind it is graded).
findings.location_wrong: The completion half is exactly located (polar_alignment_screen_parts/_completion_panel.dart). The HISTORY half is wrong and I disproved it by pixel: the finding says the 1800" history row is 'stamped with a green checkmark ... +0%'. It is not. _history_panel.dart:222-227 grades the tick `finalTotalError < 60 ? colors.success : colors.warning` and :245-259 grades the badge `improvementPercent > 50 ? colors.success : colors.info`, so at 1800"/+0% the row renders an AMBER tick and a BLUE badge - see the 3x crop /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-34b.png, where my 1800" row is amber+blue directly above a 0"/+100% row that is green+green. A fixer told 'the history row is green' would change already-correct code.

findings.title: Polar alignment computes and reports azimuth/altitude error at latitude 0, longitude 0 when no observing location is set
findings.what_happened: With no observing location configured (app_settings observer_latitude=0.0, observer_longitude=0.0; Equipment's readiness panel is actively flagging 'No observing location set'), I started TPPA and it ran all three points and produced concrete corrections - 'Azimuth Left 427.6"', 'Altitude Up 2287.9"', final 1800.0". The az/alt decomposition of a polar-axis error is a function of site latitude; at lat 0 the pole sits on the horizon, so every number the wizard printed is the correction for an observer on the equator, not for the user. The native layer has an explicit guard for this (polar_align/mod.rs:390-399 returns 'Polar alignment requires observer latitude/longitude...') but it only fires when the location is None, and the app installs a (0,0) location at startup - app.log: 'Setting observer location: lat=0, lon=0, elev=0' - so the guard can never fire.
findings.expected: Starting polar alignment with no site set must be refused with 'Set your observing location first' (the wizard already refuses on a disconnected camera, a disconnected mount and an unavailable solver), or the site must be part of the pre-flight checklist shown on the idle screen. It must never silently substitute 0,0.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, do not set an observing location. Equipment -> connect Simulated Camera + Mount. Imaging -> Mount tab -> Three-Point Polar Alignment -> Start Alignment. Verify with: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/data/skotiq.db "select key,value from app_settings where key like 'observer_%'" -> observer_latitude|0.0, observer_longitude|0.0.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-115.png (corrections printed), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-116.png (Final error 1800.0 arcseconds), /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log line 80092 'Setting observer location: lat=0, lon=0, elev=0'. Native guard that is bypassed: native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/polar_align/mod.rs:390.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/polar_alignment/polar_alignment_screen.dart:59-121 (_startAlignment pre-flight has camera/mount/solver checks but no site check); native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/state.rs get_observer_location + the startup path that sets 0,0
findings.proposed_fix: Stop materialising a (0,0) observer location: leave it None until the user sets one, so the existing native guard fires. Add a site check to _startAlignment with the same snackbar treatment as the camera/mount checks, and show it in the idle checklist ('Set your observing location').
findings.verdict_reasoning: Every load-bearing link verified independently. (1) No site: app_settings observer_latitude|0.0, observer_longitude|0.0, and Equipment readiness flags 'No observing location set' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-16.png). (2) Startup installs a real (0,0): app.log line 17 'Setting observer location: lat=0, lon=0, elev=0', from set_observer_location in native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/state.rs:355-364. (3) The native guard the finding names is therefore dead code in this state: polar_align/mod.rs:389-399 only fails when ctx.latitude/longitude are None AND device_ops.get_observer_location() returns None - with (0,0) installed it returns Some((0,0)) and the wizard proceeds. (4) Dart pre-flight has no site check: polar_alignment_screen.dart:59-120 (_startAlignment) validates camera connection, mount connection and plateSolveServiceProvider.ensureSolverAvailable(), nothing else. (5) Live: I started All-Sky polar alignment with no site set and it ran, plate-solved and entered the adjust phase (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-28.png) - not refused. Az/alt decomposition of a polar-axis error is latitude-dependent, so every correction printed is for an equatorial observer.

findings.title: All-Sky polar alignment reticle says "Within acceptance - hold steady" and 0.0" before a single frame has been taken
findings.what_happened: On the idle All-Sky screen (Start Alignment button showing, status line 'Ready to start polar alignment', and the Azimuth/Altitude/Total readouts all showing '--'), the target reticle in the right rail draws a green centred dot with the caption '0.0\"' and 'Within acceptance - hold steady'. No image has been captured and no solve has run; the app is asserting a perfect polar alignment purely because its error value is null/zero-initialised.
findings.expected: With no measurement the reticle must show no marker and read '--' / 'Not measured', exactly like the Azimuth/Altitude/Total tiles 12 px below it already do. 'Within acceptance' is the single most consequential sentence on this screen and it must only ever follow a solve.
findings.repro: Imaging -> Mount -> Three-Point Polar Alignment -> select the All-Sky segment -> (if a previous result is showing, press Restart). Read the right rail: green 0.0\" 'Within acceptance - hold steady' above 'Azimuth -- / Altitude -- / Total --'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-126.png (full screen: idle intro, 'Ready to start polar alignment', totals '--', reticle green '0.0\"' 'Within acceptance - hold steady'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-127.png (reticle close-up).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/polar_alignment/widgets/all_sky_target_reticle.dart (renders from a non-nullable error defaulting to 0) fed by _right_panel.dart
findings.proposed_fix: Make the reticle take a nullable error and render an explicit unmeasured state; gate the acceptance caption on phase != idle && a solve has landed.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced first try on a fresh profile with no prior run to leak state. Imaging -> Mount -> Three-Point Polar Alignment -> All-Sky: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-27.png shows the intro copy, footer 'Ready to start polar alignment' with a Start Alignment button, Azimuth/Altitude/Total all '--', and in the same rail a green centred marker captioned '0.0"' / 'Within acceptance - hold steady'. No exposure and no solve had run. Contrast shot proving the mechanism: after pressing Start (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-28.png) the same reticle correctly reads 'Waiting for first plate solve...'. P1 held: an operator glancing at the rail can read a perfect polar alignment off a wizard that has measured nothing.
findings.location_wrong: Symptom and file family are right, but the actionable file is the CALLER, not the reticle. _right_panel.dart:24-31 passes `state.currentError?.azimuthError ?? 0.0` / `?? 0.0` and sets `waitingForFirstFrame: state.phase == PolarAlignPhase.adjusting && state.currentError == null` - so in the IDLE phase the honest mode is switched off and the widget computes totalError=0 <= threshold. all_sky_target_reticle.dart:96-108 is only the renderer; it already has a correct 'Waiting for first plate solve...' mode that simply is not requested.

findings.title: All-Sky reticle labels collide: the error marker, the az/alt caption and the "Dn" compass label are drawn on top of each other

In one SizedBox(size,size) Stack: (1) the caption Column is 'Positioned(bottom: 8, left: 0, right: 0)' (:92-95) with a 22px total-error Text over an 11px 'Az ... Alt ...' Text (:112-125), so the az/alt line sits at roughly y = size-22 .. size-8, centred. findings.title: An aborted polar alignment is written to Alignment History as a success with a green "+97%" improvement badge
findings.what_happened: I started All-Sky polar alignment, let it iterate for ~2 minutes without touching the mount (impossible to touch - it is a simulator), then pressed Stop. The status line correctly read 'Polar alignment stopped'. But a row was still committed to polar_alignment_history and the Alignment History panel now shows 'Today 10:41 / Final: 1376\"' with a green checkmark and a green '+97%' badge. Nothing was adjusted, the user cancelled, and the residual is still 1376\" (23 arcmin). The '97% improvement' is an artefact of the first iteration's noisy 40104\" measurement being taken as 'initial'.
findings.expected: A cancelled run must either not be persisted, or be persisted and displayed as 'Stopped' with a neutral icon and no improvement badge. Improvement must be computed against a stable initial measurement, not the first noisy sample, and must not be reported at all for a run in which the user made no adjustment.
findings.repro: Polar Alignment -> All-Sky -> Start Alignment -> wait ~2 min -> Stop. Scroll the left column to Alignment History. Cross-check: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/data/skotiq.db 'select id,initial_total_error,final_total_error,auto_completed,completed_at from polar_alignment_history' -> row 2: 40104.58|1376.13|0 (auto_completed=0, i.e. threshold never met) yet completed_at is populated.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-132.png (history: 'Today 10:41 Final: 1376\"' green tick, green +97%); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-131.png ('Polar alignment stopped', Total 1376.1\" in red); DB row 2 above.
findings.where: the polar alignment history writer (run finalisation) + packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/polar_alignment/polar_alignment_screen_parts/_history_panel.dart row styling
findings.proposed_fix: Record a terminal status (completed / stopped / failed) on the history row and render it; suppress the improvement badge when auto_completed=0 and no adjustment was detected.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own run and my own numbers. All-Sky -> Start Alignment, let it plate-solve 11 iterations against the simulators without touching anything, then pressed Stop. Footer read 'Polar alignment stopped' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-29.png) - and a row was still committed: polar_alignment_history -> 1|523.692587689665|0.0|0|1785687175|1785687293, auto_completed=0 with completed_at populated. The Alignment History panel (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-30.png) then rendered 'Today 12:14 / Final: 0"' with a green checkmark and a green '+100%' badge for a run the user cancelled and in which nothing was adjusted. The improvement figure is exactly the artefact described: my series ran 31421.6" -> 95942.4" -> 0.0" -> ... -> 16688.0", pure sample noise, and 'initial' is whichever noisy sample landed first. Persistence-on-cancel is deliberate in source: polar_alignment_provider.dart stopAlignment() calls _saveHistoryOnce() at :717-733 with autoCompleted defaulting to false, and the history panel has no 'stopped' presentation at all.
findings.location_wrong: One styling detail in the evidence is wrong: the finding says the 1376" row carried a GREEN checkmark. _history_panel.dart:222-227 colours the icon `finalTotalError < 60 ? colors.success : colors.warning`, so at 1376" that tick renders AMBER. The green element at that value is only the improvement badge. What actually lies is the ICON SHAPE (autoCompleted ? target : check - a cancelled run still gets a checkmark) and the badge, not the tick colour.

findings.title: All-Sky alignment shows a drift-derived error with no indication of how long the drift baseline is
findings.what_happened: All-Sky measures polar error from the drift between a baseline solve and the current solve (native all_sky_polar/mod.rs keeps the baseline fixed and re-solves every 3 s). Its precision is therefore entirely a function of elapsed baseline, but the screen never shows elapsed time, iteration count, or a confidence indicator. In my run the headline number went 0.0\" (green, 'Within acceptance') at ~8 s, then 40104\" (11 degrees) at the next sample, then settled near 1376\". A user watching only the reticle would have believed all three.
findings.expected: Show elapsed baseline time and iteration count next to the error, and withhold the acceptance verdict until the baseline is long enough for the number to mean anything (SharpCap's drift routine does exactly this).
findings.repro: Polar Alignment -> All-Sky -> Start Alignment; watch the right-rail Azimuth/Altitude/Total tiles from the first solve onward.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-130.png (Azimuth 0.0\" Altitude 0.0\" in green a few seconds in) vs DB row 2 initial_total_error=40104.58 vs /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-131.png (Total 1376.1\") - three different answers for the same untouched mount inside two minutes, with nothing on screen to rank them.
findings.proposed_fix: Publish elapsed-baseline seconds and sample count in the progress event and render them; gate the green 'Within acceptance' caption on a minimum baseline.

findings.title: Flat Frame Wizard captures at a different camera offset than the Imaging screen (10 vs 50) and never shows which gain/offset it will use
findings.what_happened: At 10:46 the Imaging screen's Camera tab showed 'Gain (0-600) 100 / Offset (0-255) 50', and the app's own light-frame path commands offset 50 (app.log 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50)'). At 10:50 I ran the Flat Frame Wizard on the same camera in the same session, and every one of its seven exposures was commanded as 'gain=Some(100), offset=Some(10)'. The Flat Wizard UI displays no gain or offset anywhere - Quick Capture shows only Filter, Histogram Target, Tolerance and Frame Count - so nothing warns the user. Flats taken at a different offset from the lights carry the wrong bias pedestal and the app's own library matcher refuses them: flat_library_dao.dart:132 states 'gain, offset, and binning must match exactly'.
findings.expected: The flat wizard must capture with the same gain/offset the light frames will use, and it must display them (NINA shows gain/offset/binning on the flat wizard panel and lets you override them). If the two surfaces genuinely have different sources of truth, that is the bug; at minimum the wizard has to show the values it is about to command.
findings.repro: Equipment -> connect Simulated Camera. Imaging -> Camera tab -> read Gain/Offset. Imaging -> Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture -> Start Capture -> choose a folder -> Continue. Then: grep 'gain=Some' /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-136.png (Camera tab: Gain 100, Offset 50). /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log 14:50:34-14:51:03: seven lines 'Starting <t>s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(10), bin=1x1'. Earlier light path in the same profile: 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/flat_wizard_service.dart:314-323 (offset = profileDefaultOffset ?? currentOffset ?? status.offset) vs the imaging capture path; UI: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/flat_wizard/ (no gain/offset surface)
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the flat capture config from the same source the light capture uses, and render 'Gain 100 - Offset 50 - Bin 1x1' on the wizard panel with an override affordance.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Both halves reproduced in one session on one camera. Imaging -> Camera tab reads 'Gain (0-600) 100' and 'Offset (0-255) 50' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-35.png). Light-frame path on the same camera minutes earlier: app.log 16:09:40 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'. Flat wizard Quick Capture run on the same camera: seven consecutive lines from 16:25:58 'Starting <t>s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(10), bin=1x1'. So lights get offset 50 and flats get offset 10 in the same session. The UI half is also true: Quick Capture shows only Filter, Histogram Target, Tolerance and Frame Count (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-37.png) - no gain, no offset, no override. Cited location right and I pinned the divergence: flat_wizard_service.dart:321 `offset = profileDefaultOffset ?? currentOffset ?? status?.offset`, fed from flat_wizard_provider.dart:144-149. In this profile equipment_profiles.default_offset is NULL, so it falls through to the camera's live/driver-reported offset (10), while the light path uses app_settings default_offset=50. Two sources of truth, exactly as claimed.

findings.title: Flat wizard's "Flat capture failed - no frames were saved" gives no reason and no next step

Exposure ramped 2.39s (ADU 1049) -> 13.79s (ADU 1198) -> 30.00s (ADU 1364), status chip 'Failed', red banner 'Flat capture failed - no frames were saved.' - within 3 ADU of the reported 1361. findings.title: Flat wizard cannot capture a flat when a filter move is needed - its wheel move neither takes effect nor is confirmed, while the same move works from Equipment
findings.what_happened: Every Quick Capture run that needs a wheel move dies with 'filter wheel did not confirm position 0 within 15s - run stopped.' The native call reports success in the same millisecond - app.log: '[API] api_filterwheel_set_position called: device_id=sim_filterwheel_1, position=0' immediately followed by '[API] Filter wheel position set successfully' - but the Dart filterWheelStateProvider the wizard polls (flat_wizard_provider.dart:1372-1383, waiting for !isMoving && currentPosition == position) never reports the new position, so the wizard fails closed after 15 s. Crucially the wheel itself is fine: issuing the SAME position-0 command from the Equipment screen's filter-wheel card moved it and the card updated to 'L / #1' within ~5 s. So the move works everywhere except from the flat wizard, and after the wizard's two attempts the wheel was still sitting on Ha/#5. The only flat runs that ever reached the exposure stage were the ones where the wheel already happened to be at the target and the move was skipped (line 1346). Zero flats were written across four attempts: /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/flats is empty and flat_history/flat_library have 0 rows.
findings.expected: After a successful filterWheelSetPosition the wheel state must be refreshed (event or poll) so the confirmation loop sees the new position. Failing that, the wizard must say the wheel reported success but never confirmed, and offer to proceed - not just stop.
findings.repro: Connect Simulated Camera + Simulated Filter Wheel. Imaging -> Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture -> Start Capture -> choose a folder -> Continue. Wait 15 s.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-157.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-163.png (the banner); app.log 14:57:32 and 15:01:46 (wizard commands position=0, native reports success, wheel stays on Ha); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-178.png (Equipment card still reading 'Ha / #5' twelve minutes after the wizard's second attempt) vs /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-181.png (same card reading 'L / #1' five seconds after the Equipment dropdown issued the identical position=0 at 15:14:03); sqlite3 ... 'select count(*) from flat_history' = 0 and 'find /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/flats -type f' returns nothing.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/flat_wizard_provider.dart:1370-1394 (the confirmation loop) and whatever should refresh filterWheelStateProvider after filterWheelSetPosition
findings.proposed_fix: Re-read the wheel status from the backend inside the poll loop instead of relying solely on a pushed event, and emit a position-changed event from the filter wheel driver after a successful set.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with the wheel at Ha and the wizard asked for B. app.log 16:20:43.804816 'api_filterwheel_set_position ... position=3' immediately followed at 16:20:43.804835 by 'Filter wheel position set successfully' - and 15 s later the wizard failed closed: 'B: filter wheel did not confirm position 3 within 15s - run stopped.' with the run strip flipping to Failed (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-44.png). The asymmetry is real and I verified both directions: driving the SAME wheel from the Imaging filter chip row worked (position=4 at 16:18:47; chip row and the wizard's dropdown both then showed Ha), whereas after the wizard's move the app still believed the wheel was on Ha (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-46.png and wiz-47.png) even though the driver had accepted position 3. Root cause confirmed with its counterpart: DeviceService's changeFilter path calls _verifyFilterWheelPosition (control_helpers.dart:314-361), which polls `_backend.getFilterWheelStatus(deviceId)` and pushes the result into the provider via filterWheelNotifier.updatePosition/setMoving - while flat_wizard_provider.dart:1351-1382 calls filterWheelSetPosition directly and then polls `ref.read(filterWheelStateProvider)` with nothing in that loop ever fetching status, so it can never change. Outcome matches: zero flats written (0 files under /tmp/ns-audit/v-wizards/flats; flat_history count 0). Worse than reported: the stale state also makes the NEXT run unsafe - my second run skipped the move and exposed seven frames labelled Ha while the driver sat on position 3 (B).

findings.title: The Smart Night dashboard prompt never appears even with its toggle on and every documented precondition met
findings.what_happened: Settings -> Sequencer -> Smart Night Defaults -> 'Dashboard auto-prompt' ('Show the Smart Night prompt on the dashboard when your equipment is ready') is ON by default and I confirmed the toggle is blue/on. I then satisfied every gate the card checks (smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-127): profile focal length 550 mm and aperture 100 mm saved (equipmentReady), observing location 40.0 / -105.0 and not 0,0, no sequence running, nothing dismissed on a fresh profile, and I waited more than four minutes - well past the 60 s readiness grace. The bottom-centre prompt never appeared, on the briefing dashboard or the cockpit dashboard.
findings.expected: With the toggle on and equipment ready the prompt should slide in from the bottom centre. Either it shows, or the setting should not promise it.
findings.repro: Fresh profile -> Settings -> Location: 40 / -105 -> Equipment -> Edit Profile -> focal length 550, aperture 100 -> connect the four simulators -> Dashboard -> wait 4 minutes.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-212.png (dashboard right after connecting), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-213.png (bottom strip 60 s later), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-214.png (four minutes in - no prompt anywhere); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-217.png and rw-218.png (the 'Dashboard auto-prompt' row and its toggle, on).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-144 - the two remaining suppressors are the 60 s grace rebuild (_equipmentReadyGraceElapsed / _graceTimer) and 'if (draftAsync.isLoading || draftAsync.valueOrNull != null) return SizedBox.shrink()' on pendingSmartNightDraftProvider; a provider that never leaves loading would hide the card forever with no trace.
findings.proposed_fix: Log and test the two suppressors: give pendingSmartNightDraftProvider a timeout and treat an unresolved lookup as 'no draft', and assert the grace timer schedules a rebuild. Caveat: the equipment on this profile was connected via Discovery rather than assigned to the profile ('0 devices'), which the card does not check but a related provider might.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and root-caused. Fresh v2-wizards profile: Settings -> Location 40.0 / -105.0 (scratch DB app_settings observer_latitude=40.0, observer_longitude=-105.0), Edit Profile focal length 550 / aperture 100 (equipment_profiles row 1|My Equipment|550.0|100.0), sim camera + mount connected, no sequence running, nothing dismissed, smartNightAutoPromptEnabled defaults true (app_settings.dart:384). Sat on the dashboard >4.5 minutes; the a11y tree never contained 'Hardware ready' or 'Smart Night will choose'. ROOT CAUSE: smart_night_prompt_card.dart:21 declares 'final smartNightPromptNowProvider = Provider<DateTime>((ref) => DateTime.now());' - a non-autoDispose Riverpod Provider, so DateTime.now() is evaluated once and cached for the container's life. _equipmentReadyGraceElapsed (:297-326) then does '_equipmentReadySince ??= now' and 'final elapsed = now.difference(_equipmentReadySince!)', which is ALWAYS Duration.zero, so readyGraceElapsed is permanently false, canPlan (:118-122) is permanently false, and the card returns SizedBox.shrink() forever. The 60 s _graceTimer fires once, setState rebuilds, elapsed is still zero, and because _graceTimer is left non-null the '??=' never re-arms it. 'where' (smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-144) is accurate - :118-127 is exactly the canPlan/baseShouldShow block and :139-144 the draftAsync guard.
